title: Core-periphery Partitioning and Quantum Annealing

problem.claim: The task is to compute a core-periphery partition for an undirected network and identify an associated optimal partitioning.

gap.claim: The QUBO formulation uses a full matrix even for sparse networks, limiting the available problem dimension for quantum annealing.

contributions.claim: A kernel is proposed to quantify success in computing a core-periphery partition for an undirected network.
A sparsified version of the original QUBO is developed and tested to increase the available problem dimension for a quantum annealer.
The new objective function is used to assess a quantum annealer and compare it with existing heuristic core-periphery partitioning methods.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Quantum annealing is performed on a commercially available D-Wave machine.
Results are provided on synthetic and real data sets.
The authors conclude that the QUBO/quantum annealing approach offers benefits for optimizing the proposed quantity of interest.

narrative_sequence.summary: A new kernel is proposed to quantify success in core-periphery partitioning.
The optimal partitioning is formulated as a QUBO problem suitable for quantum annealing.
The objective is used to evaluate quantum annealing and compare it with heuristic methods on a D-Wave machine.
Because the QUBO is dense even for sparse networks, a sparsified version is developed and tested to increase problem dimension.
Synthetic and real-data results are reported, with the authors concluding that the approach benefits optimization of the proposed quantity.

source_observation.claim: A sparse underlying network can still produce a full-matrix QUBO formulation.

interpretation.claim: The representation used for optimization can determine hardware-feasible problem size independently of input sparsity.

application.claim: When mapping sparse problems to specialized hardware, inspect and sparsify the optimization representation to increase usable dimension.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that sparsification preserves solution quality or improves performance across all network types.

unknowns: Exact definition of the kernel and objective function
Quantum annealing parameters and hardware configuration
Characteristics and sizes of the synthetic and real data sets
